Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

from preposition

from a place or a person

classical

Vulg. Ps. 112 (113), 3: Ā sōlis ortū ūsque ad occāsum
Gell. 15.7.3: cum ā mē abes

ā, ab (+ ablative)

preposition with the ablative; ā before consonants, ab before vowels and h

from (away from a place or a person)

From the side of a place or a person: ā mē, from me; ā Rōmā, from the neighbourhood of Rome. Abs tē is the form of comedy and of Cicero until about 54 BC (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • ē, ex (+ ablative) — from (out of)

    preposition with the ablative; ex before vowels and often before consonants, ē only before consonants · classical · Sen. Ep. 35.3: venit ad nōs ex iīs quōs amāmus … gaudium

    From inside a thing, or from among a number: see out of.

  • dē (+ ablative) — from, down from

    preposition with the ablative · classical · Cic. Att. 12.2.2: dē viā rēctā ad mē

    From a place or a surface, often downward: dē viā, from the road; dē mēnsā, off the table (see off).

  • domō, rūre; Rōmā (ablative alone) — from home, from the country; from Rome

    ablative without a preposition · classical · Verg. A. 8.113–114: quī genus? unde domō?

    Names of towns and small islands, domus and rūs take no preposition: Rōmā proficīscī, set out from Rome; domō exīre, leave the house.

Examples

  • Ā sōlis ortū ūsque ad occāsum laudābile nōmen Dominī.

    From the rising of the sun to its setting the name of the Lord is to be praised.Vulg. Ps. 112 (113), 3

  • jam tē vidēbō et quidem, ut spērō, dē viā rēctā ad mē

    I shall see you soon, and, I hope, straight from the road to my houseCic. Att. 12.2.2

  • venit ad nōs ex iīs quōs amāmus etiam absentibus gaudium

    joy comes to us from those we love, even when they are awaySen. Ep. 35.3

  • quō tenditis? inquit; quī genus? unde domō?

    “Where are you heading?” he said. “Who are your people? Where are you from?”Verg. A. 8.113–114

See also out of, away from, off, to.
